## Overview

The [APSIM](https://www.apsim.info/) crop modelling platform requires a site meteorological
file containing daily weather observations with specific variable names, units, and header
metadata. `ag5_apsim()` automates this workflow:

1. Extracts the required AgERA5 variables from locally downloaded `.nc` files.
2. Applies unit conversions (Kelvin → °C, J/m²/day → MJ/m²/day).
3. Computes the site constants `tav` and `amp`.
4. Writes a ready-to-use `.met` file (classic APSIM) or `.csv` + constants file (APSIM Next Generation).

## Variable mapping

| APSIM column | AgERA5 variable | Statistic | Unit conversion |
|---|---|---|---|
| `maxt` | Temperature-Air-2m | Max-24h | K → °C |
| `mint` | Temperature-Air-2m | Min-24h | K → °C |
| `rain` | Precipitation-Flux | — | none (mm/day) |
| `radn` | Solar-Radiation-Flux | — | J/m²/day ÷ 1 000 000 → MJ/m²/day |
| `wind` | Wind-Speed-10m | Mean | none (m/s) |
| `vp` | Vapour-Pressure | Mean | none (hPa) |
| `rh` | Relative-Humidity-2m | — | none (%) |

`maxt`, `mint`, `rain`, and `radn` are the four variables required by APSIM for all
simulations. `wind`, `vp`, and `rh` are optional but used by several crop modules.

## Site constants: `tav` and `amp`

APSIM `.met` files carry two header constants derived from the weather record:

- **`tav`** — annual average temperature (°C), computed as the mean of `(maxt + mint) / 2`
  across all days.
- **`amp`** — half the range between the warmest and coolest monthly mean temperatures (°C),
  computed as `(max(monthly_mean_temp) - min(monthly_mean_temp)) / 2`.

`ag5_apsim()` computes both constants automatically from the extracted data.

## Controlling which variables are extracted

The `variables` argument accepts three forms:

| Value | Variables extracted |
|---|---|
| `"all"` (default) | maxt, mint, rain, radn, wind, vp, rh |
| `"required"` | maxt, mint, rain, radn |
| character vector | any subset, e.g. `c("maxt", "mint", "rain", "radn", "wind")` |

## Examples

### Return a data.frame (no file written)

When `filename = NULL` (the default), `ag5_apsim()` returns an annotated `data.frame`
and prints the site constants to the console.

```{r eval = FALSE}
library(ag5Tools)

met <- ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),   # lon, lat — Arusha, Tanzania
  start_date = "2015-01-01",
  end_date   = "2015-12-31",
  variables  = "required",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data"
)

head(met)
#>   year day   maxt   mint  rain      radn
#> 1 2015   1  27.43  17.89  0.00  19.42
#> 2 2015   2  28.12  18.03  0.00  20.11
#> 3 2015   3  26.78  17.61  2.34  15.73
#> ...

attr(met, "tav")
attr(met, "amp")
```

### Write a classic APSIM .met file

Set `filename` to a path without extension; `ag5_apsim()` appends `.met`.

```{r eval = FALSE}
ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2015-01-01",
  end_date   = "2015-12-31",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha_2015",
  format     = "classic"
)
```

The output file `arusha_2015.met` looks like:

```
! Generated by ag5Tools
latitude = -3.37 (degrees)
longitude = 36.68 (degrees)
tav = 20.34 (oC)
amp = 1.72 (oC)

year day radn maxt mint rain wind vp rh
() () (MJ/m2) (oC) (oC) (mm) (m/s) (hPa) (%)
2015 1 19.42 27.43 17.89 0.00 2.3 18.4 71
2015 2 20.11 28.12 18.03 0.00 1.9 17.9 68
...
```

### Write an APSIM Next Generation file

For APSIM Next Generation, use `format = "apsimng"`. This writes two files:
`arusha_2015.csv` (data) and `arusha_2015_constants.txt` (site metadata).

```{r eval = FALSE}
ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2015-01-01",
  end_date   = "2015-12-31",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha_2015",
  format     = "apsimng"
)
```

### Extract only required variables

```{r eval = FALSE}
ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2015-01-01",
  end_date   = "2015-12-31",
  variables  = "required",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha_2015_min",
  format     = "classic"
)
```

### Extract a custom subset of variables

```{r eval = FALSE}
ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2015-01-01",
  end_date   = "2015-12-31",
  variables  = c("maxt", "mint", "rain", "radn", "wind"),
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha_2015_wind",
  format     = "classic"
)
```

### Download missing files automatically

If AgERA5 files for the requested period are not yet on disk, set `download = TRUE`.
The function will fetch any missing files before extracting, using the location derived
from `coords` as the bounding box.

```{r eval = FALSE}
ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2015-01-01",
  end_date   = "2015-12-31",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha_2015",
  download   = TRUE
)
```

### Relative humidity time-of-day

`rh` is extracted at a specific time of day. The default is `"09h"`. Use `rh_time`
to change this.

```{r eval = FALSE}
ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2015-01-01",
  end_date   = "2015-12-31",
  variables  = c("maxt", "mint", "rain", "radn", "rh"),
  rh_time    = "12h",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha_2015_rh12"
)
```

## Multi-year records

To build a multi-year `.met` file, extend the date range. `ag5_apsim()` handles
leap years correctly via R's `seq.Date()`.

```{r eval = FALSE}
ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2010-01-01",
  end_date   = "2020-12-31",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha_2010_2020",
  format     = "classic"
)
```

## Integration with the apsimx R package

The [`apsimx`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=apsimx) package (Miguez, 2022) lets you
run and edit APSIM Next Generation simulations entirely from R. Its built-in examples —
including a ready-to-run Wheat simulation — are documented in the
[apsimx vignette](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/apsimx/vignettes/apsimx.html).

The example below shows only the ag5Tools step: generating a `.met` file for the Wheat
example site (**Dalby, Queensland, Australia**, lon = 151.26, lat = −27.18, the classic
APSIM benchmark location) and then replacing the weather file in the simulation using
`edit_apsimx()`. Everything else — soil, management, crop parameters — remains exactly
as documented in the apsimx vignette.

### Step 1: generate the met file with ag5Tools

```{r eval = FALSE}
library(ag5Tools)

ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(151.26, -27.18),    # Dalby, QLD
  start_date = "1990-01-01",
  end_date   = "2020-12-31",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/dalby_agera5",
  format     = "classic"
)
# writes: C:/apsim/dalby_agera5.met
```

### Step 2: swap the weather file in the apsimx Wheat example

```{r eval = FALSE}
library(apsimx)

# Locate the built-in Wheat example that ships with apsimx
ex.dir <- system.file("extdata", package = "apsimx")

# Replace the weather node with the AgERA5 met file and write to a working directory
edit_apsimx(
  "Wheat.apsimx",
  src.dir = ex.dir,
  wrt.dir = "C:/apsim",
  node    = "Weather",
  value   = "C:/apsim/dalby_agera5.met"
)
```

The edited `Wheat.apsimx` in `C:/apsim` now uses AgERA5 climate data. Run it and retrieve
results with `apsimx()` as shown in the
[apsimx documentation](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/apsimx/vignettes/apsimx.html).

```{r eval = FALSE}
sim <- apsimx("Wheat.apsimx", src.dir = "C:/apsim", value = "report")
head(sim)
```
